narrative.overview:
The dashboard is a water-routing board, not a card grid. A single channel carries the measured trace from the left edge to a NOW station, then an amber bridge reaches a fixed +15 MIN station. Everything around that channel is an instrument readout: pipeline stations down the left, decision and pump state on the right, safety and provenance along the foot. The metaphor stops at the gauge; buttons, chips and lists are ordinary web controls a presenter can use without decoding a theme.

Legibility beats decoration. The lecture-hall context means one screen must survive a projector and a skeptical examiner: freshness first, then state, then forecast, then decision, then the device's own pump report. One humanist system sans carries every role, and every number is tabular so live updates never shift the grid. Nothing loads from a CDN, and one 320 ms motion on the forecast dot is the only non-user-triggered movement.
keyCharacteristics: One stretched channel with a measured trace, an amber forecast bridge and two labelled stations.
A five-station state chain that writes every state out in words.
Flat enamel panels separated by single hairlines, never rounded cards or soft shadows.
Live age, weather source, model quality and safety limits visible without navigation.

rules.name: The One Gauge Rule
rules.body: The canal metaphor lives only in the channel and its stations. Controls stay standard; no pump button becomes a sluice lever.

rules.name: The Freshness Rule
rules.body: The last-reading age and clock sit in the top bar before the forecast is read. A stale sensor is named, never implied.

rules.name: The Measured Rule
rules.body: Colour never carries state alone. Every state, warning and pump condition is written out in words, so the board remains readable without colour vision.

rules.name: The Numbers Rule
rules.body: All telemetry uses tabular numerals. A live reading must change its digits without moving the label beside it.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No card floats. If a surface needs emphasis, change its tone or its one-pixel border, never its shadow.

dos: Do keep the amber +15 MIN station on the gauge and its label in the HTML overlay.
Do show the last-reading age and clock before the forecast value.
Do use tabular numerals and 1px rules at every breakpoint.
Do keep prefers-reduced-motion honoured by removing the forecast-dot transition.
Do print SENSOR_STALE, WEATHER_STALE and MANUAL_OVERRIDE as words beside the station chain.
donts: Don't add rounded cards, soft drop shadows, gradients or CDN fonts.
Don't put SVG text inside the stretched gauge; it distorts at mobile widths.
Don't carry the canal metaphor into buttons, chips or lists.
Don't encode pump or AI state in colour alone.
Don't invent a confidence percentage; show spread and holdout error.
